Inspect or edit the structured CSV

Repeat the same header fields for each invoice line. Use line numbers starting at 1. A blank PO is held as an unmatched reference; the original blank is retained. Invoice files cannot supply expense accounts or cost centers.

Previewing does not write the journal. Staging creates invoice documents only; AP posting, payment approval and settlement remain separate. Staging the guided example replaces a different local purchasing journal only after explicit confirmation. Maintenance and work checkpoints are preserved and may refer to prior purchasing records.

Give every exception an owner.

Queue counts are distinct invoice headers using their primary review reason. A document can have additional line-level reasons. Multi-line header amounts are not repeated as cost-center totals.

File contract, atomic staging and limits

One CSV data row is one invoice line. The exact columns are documentId, entityId, supplierId, invoiceReference, currency, headerNet, lineNumber, poLineId, quantity and unitPrice. Entity is SYN-CO-01. The file supports 200 rows, up to 50 invoice headers and 1–20 contiguous lines per header, within 256 KiB.

Amounts use exact cents and quantities use whole units. Header conflicts, malformed CSV, duplicate line numbers and unsupported columns reject the new preview while preserving the prior valid result. Header/line net mismatches and unknown supplier/PO/currency references become owned document holds. No account is guessed from the vendor.

The full candidate batch is evaluated together with existing pending documents. All duplicate and competing candidates are held rather than giving the first input row priority. Existing documents whose review status would change are disclosed. The preview is checked against the current journal before staging; a changed journal requires another preview. The complete batch stages atomically, and stable command IDs prevent duplicate retries.

These are fictional structured documents, not PDF/email ingestion, OCR or AI extraction. All processing stays in the browser under the existing no-network content policy. Roles illustrate responsibilities, not authenticated access.
